primary_cross_channel.question: On calendar days carrying at least one frozen Blue Book STARLIKE report, is the POSS-I candidate rate elevated on nights when Palomar actually observed?
primary_cross_channel.lag_read: No isolated exact-day or post-event rate peak is visible across the frozen -7..+7 crude lag profile. The largest local crude ratio occurs at lag -2 rather than on the STARLIKE date, which argues against interpreting the nominal exact-day IRR as a specific shared trigger.

D1_SOLAR_F107_HIGH.action: No interpolation, fallback or replacement after outcome.

D5_MAJOR_METEOR_SHOWER_GREGORIAN_PROXY.boundary: This remains only a fixed Gregorian proxy; no meteor attribution would have been admitted without historical solar-longitude reconstruction even if significant.

aggregate_verdict.interpretation: Within the v1 frozen families, neither Blue Book STARLIKE timing nor POSS-I conditional candidate rate shows a multiplicity-surviving common association with sunspot-high days, geomagnetic storms or the major-meteor-shower proxy. Lunar extremes do not show a significant POSS-I rate effect. F10.7 was not tested because historical source coverage was incomplete.

what_this_rules_out: A simple same-day Blue Book STARLIKE -> elevated POSS-I candidate-rate relationship is not established in the open reconstruction.
High sunspot-number days are not a common STARLIKE/POSS-I discriminator in this test.
Kp>=5 or Kp>=7 geomagnetic-storm days are not a common STARLIKE/POSS-I discriminator in this test.
The preregistered fixed-date major meteor-shower proxy does not explain or predict the two layers.
Dark or bright Moon conditions do not produce a significant residual POSS-I candidate-rate effect after the frozen nuisance controls.
what_remains_open: Exact timestamped historical H-alpha solar-flare events rather than broad solar-cycle proxies.
Row-complete rocket, missile, high-altitude balloon and air-defense activity calendars with explicit coverage denominators.
Palomar-local historical weather/cloud/visibility data with station-lineage completeness gates.
Historical meteor-shower solar-longitude reconstruction rather than fixed Gregorian dates.
Spatial coincidence: whether a human report direction/location and a Palomar plate footprint could geometrically refer to a compatible sky region.
Blue Book source-card validation and complete-denominator reconstruction.

priority_order: NCEI Palomar-area weather station lineage and daily/hourly coverage
next_recommended_stage.rule: Acquire and freeze completeness/provenance before testing any new association.

authority_decision.reason: JPFM-3A is an executed open research result with a null cross-event admission outcome; it does not create a new canonical physical explanation.
